titre: Former Blade Director Reveals What Went Wrong With The Ill-Fated Marvel Movie
chapo: "It was funny and strange to start casting and building without a proper script," director Bassam Tariq said of his work on the canceled Blade movie
extrait: "It was funny and strange to start casting and building without a proper script" Director Bassam Tariq, who was previously attached to direct the Mahershala Ali Blade movie that never came to fruition, was candid that the lack of a strong, complete script caused the Marvel Cinematic Universe movie to fall apart before it even started shooting. The production timeline of the MCU Blade movie was brutal. It was first announced at San Diego Comic-Con in 2019 and was supposed to come out in 2023. Tariq signed on as director in 2021, and pre-production seemed in full swing by the summer of 2022, but Tariq stepped away from directing that September. While director Yenn Demange was then attached to the project, the 2023 actor's strike and ongoing production problems pushed the movie back even further. Demange left the project in June 2024, and by 2025, the film had completely fizzled out. Ali has shared that he has moved on from wanting to play Blade, and he and Tariq subsequently collaborated on the action movie Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother. Speaking to The New Arab about the movie, Tariq was pretty transparent about why he walked away from making it. "It was funny and strange to start casting and building without a proper script. You're sitting there and explaining to actors what their role will be, and they just have to believe you," he explained. "That's also very dangerous because if the text comes and it doesn't add up to what you were saying, your credibility gets completely shot. All I have is my integrity, and I've been thinking about that a lot. If you're the bearer of bad news to your actors, but you're not the one making any of these decisions — and it's actually coming from a corporate entity — that's not a great way to be a director." Ultimately, Tariq's big takeaways from his work on Blade were that "life's too short to make shit films" and that he wants full control over the scripts for the movies he makes going forward. That was the case for Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother, which has received rave reviews. It's well documented that Marvel movies don't often start production with locked scripts, and major changes to the story and certain action set pieces can happen mid-production. In Blade's case, that process didn't seem to work particularly well for Tariq as a director, and the movie fell apart as a result. titre: Blade Director Says He Walked Away From Marvel's Canceled Movie Because 'Life's Too Short to Make S**t Films'
chapo: Director Bassam Tariq has opened up about why he exited Marvel's Blade movie, saying, "life's too short to make s**t films."
extrait: Director Bassam Tariq has opened up about why he exited Marvel's Blade movie, saying, "life's too short to make s**t films." The Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother filmmaker explained his reasoning for walking away from the Mahershala Ali superhero period piece during an interview with The New Arab. With just one other feature film (Mogul Mowgli) under his belt at the time, working on Blade presented quite the opportunity, but his short time attached as the flick's first director wound up being more of a learning lesson than anything else. "It was funny and strange to start casting and building without a proper script," Tariq said when asked what working in the studio system taught him. "You're sitting there and explaining to actors what their role will be, and they just have to believe you. "That's also very dangerous because if the text comes and it doesn't add up to what you were saying, your credibility gets completely shot. All I have is my integrity, and I've been thinking about that a lot." Marvel Studios announced an Ali-led Blade film in 2019 and picked Tariq to lead the charge in 2021. A little more than one year later, and the director was said to have bounced off the project, with Marvel telling The Hollywood Reporter that "shifts in our production schedule" were to blame. Today, one new director and multiple frustrated Ali updates later, and Blade has been finally, officially canceled. Marvel Cinematic Universe orchestrator Kevin Feige said the process made him feel like a "gigantic loser and failure" – an assessment Ali agreed with – but for Tariq, the decision to cut off his relationship with Blade came down to how it was impacting his relationship with the film's actors. He told The New Arab that being "the bearer of bad news to your actors" while a corporate entity makes all of the major decisions in the background is "not a great way to be a director." "I know some people can take that and run with it, but I learned I was losing credibility with my actors, and it wasn't a healthy way to operate as a filmmaker. Life's too short to make s**t films, so that was my big lesson: I have to have full control over my script. If we disagree, it's between them and me. It's quite sad because we had such high hopes for what we wanted to build." For now, as Marvel heads into another major release with next month's Avengers: Doomsday, there seems to be no sign of a live-action Blade for the MCU.
